verdict.rationale: Keycloak documents client-credentials service accounts for machine-to-machine access, so an agent can be issued its own client_id/secret or JWT credential. That credential can be restricted with role-based and fine-grained resource-level authorization policies, then validated or revoked via the introspection and revocation endpoints. Clients can also be created programmatically through dynamic client registration, the Admin REST API, or kcadm.sh. missing for 10: explicit documentation of per-client OAuth scope restriction (client scopes) in the evidence, agent-specific least-privilege guidance, and independent or hands-on corroboration of scoped machine credentials.
